desc:
Let the height of a subtree be the number of nodes on its longest downward path (an empty subtree has height 0). Call a node unbalanced if the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by more than 1.

Return how many nodes of the tree are unbalanced. A tree is height-balanced exactly when this number is 0.

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For tree = [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, -1, -1, 4, 4] the answer is 1 (only the root: its left subtree has height 3, its right one has height 1). For the chain [1, 2, -1, 3, -1, 4] the answer is 2.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: Unlike the yes/no balance check, you may not stop at the first bad node: every node has to be examined.
Each node needs only the heights of its two subtrees. Computing a height from scratch at every node is too slow on tall trees.
Go through the nodes from last to first in level order, store the height of each node, and count the nodes where the two child heights differ by more than 1.
editorial: The height of every subtree is needed by its parent, so compute heights bottom-up in one pass. At each node compare the two child heights (missing child = 0); if they differ by more than 1 increase the counter. The node height is then 1 + max(left, right).
Because the level-order array lists parents before children, walking the real nodes backwards guarantees that both child heights are ready when a node is reached. The whole solution is O(n).
